017package org.apache.juneau.petstore.console;
018
019import java.io.*;
020import java.util.*;
021
022import org.apache.juneau.commons.settings.*;
023import org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter.*;
024
025import jakarta.servlet.*;
026import jakarta.servlet.http.*;
027
028/**
029 * The {@code /petstore} API's CSRF boundary: a {@link RequestBoundaryFilter} over the framework's {@link CsrfBoundary},
030 * applied to {@code /petstore} and everything under it.
031 *
032 * <p>
033 * A browser write to the API must come from the page's own origin and carry this boundary's token in the
034 * {@code X-Csrf-Token} header.  The token travels in the header only, so every HTML {@code <form>} POST to
035 * the API is refused, the application's own included.  Requests are judged on their effective method, so
036 * {@code GET /petstore/pets/1?method=DELETE} counts as a write.  Reads are allowed, and so are non-browser writes
037 * (no {@code Origin} and no {@code Sec-Fetch-Site}) that a browser could not have sent cross-site without a CORS
038 * preflight: JSON, XML or UON bodies, and {@code PUT}, {@code DELETE} or {@code PATCH}.  A non-browser urlencoded,
039 * multipart or {@code text/plain} {@code POST} is refused.  Every refusal names its reason in the
040 * {@value RequestBoundaryFilter#REJECTION_HEADER} response header.
041 *
042 * <h5 class='section'>The token</h5>
043 * <p>
044 * The token is per process ({@link CsrfTokens#perProcess()}): the petstore has no login session, and the
045 * {@code Origin} check does the real work.  A restart invalidates the token on every open page, so reload them.  A
046 * token that leaks through a page stays valid until the restart.
047 *
048 * <p>
049 * This token is not the console's.  The console boundary ({@link PetstoreConsoleBoundary}) has its own, and each
050 * boundary refuses the other's.  The console's one write to the API, its photo upload, gets this boundary's token
051 * from the console boundary, which publishes {@link #tokenFor(HttpServletRequest)} under {@link #TOKEN_ATTRIBUTE}
052 * on every console request it allows; the page's script sends it in that header.  So a runner must
053 * give the console boundary the same instance it mounts here: a token from any other instance is refused.
054 *
055 * <p>
056 * The console page shell marks a token-bearing page {@code no-store}, and when the response is already committed it
057 * strips only its own token attributes.  So on the rare page whose buffer was flushed before the shell ran, this
058 * boundary's token can still be emitted, possibly without {@code no-store}.  That is accepted: this token is only
059 * ever published on console pages, which carry the console's token too, so on every normal path the page is already
060 * marked.
061 *
062 * <h5 class='section'>The host</h5>
063 * <p>
064 * The request's own origin is its scheme plus its {@code Host} header; forwarded headers are never read.  By default
065 * any {@code Host} is answered, which suits a loopback developer setup.  On a host served over plain HTTP, set
066 * {@value #ALLOWED_HOSTS_PROPERTY} (a system property, the environment, or any registered setting source) to the
067 * comma-separated host names the browser uses, without ports.  Every request to the API under any other {@code Host},
068 * reads included, is then answered with {@code 421}: this is the DNS-rebinding defence.  The setting is read once,
069 * when the boundary is constructed, and a malformed entry fails construction rather than being ignored.
070 *
071 * <p>
072 * Behind a TLS-terminating proxy the browser's {@code https} origin does not match the {@code http} request the
073 * container sees, so writes are refused.  Such a deployment needs the container's forwarded-header support and the
074 * framework boundary's {@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter.CsrfBoundary.OriginSource#CONTAINER CONTAINER} origin source, which this demo does not
075 * configure.
076 *
077 * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
078 * <p>
079 * In a Juneau microservice, contribute a <c>ServletFilterRegistration</c> <c>@Bean</c> just after the console
080 * boundary's, sharing the one instance with it:
081 * <p class='bjava'>
082 *    <jk>private final</jk> PetstoreApiBoundary <jf>apiBoundary</jf> = <jk>new</jk> PetstoreApiBoundary();
083 *
084 *    <ja>@Bean</ja>
085 *    <jk>public</jk> ServletFilterRegistration apiBoundary() {
086 *       <jk>return</jk> ServletFilterRegistration.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jf>apiBoundary</jf>)
087 *          .urlPatterns(PetstoreApiBoundary.<jsf>URL_PATTERN</jsf>)
088 *          .dispatcherTypes(DispatcherType.<jsf>REQUEST</jsf>)
089 *          .order(ServletFilterRegistration.<jsf>HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE</jsf> + 10)
090 *          .build();
091 *    }
092 * </p>
093 * <p>
094 * and build the console boundary with {@code new PetstoreConsoleBoundary(apiBoundary)}.  Register it for
095 * {@code REQUEST} dispatches only: an internal forward or error dispatch is not a new request from the browser.
096 */
097public class PetstoreApiBoundary implements Filter {
098
099   /** The covered path: the API resource's mount point. */
100   public static final String PATH = "/petstore";
101
102   /** The servlet URL pattern the boundary is registered under.  It matches {@link #PATH} itself and every path under it. */
103   public static final String URL_PATTERN = PATH + "/*";
104
105   /**
106    * Setting (system property, environment, or any registered source) listing the host names the API answers to:
107    * comma-separated, no ports.  Unset or blank, any host is answered.
108    */
109   public static final String ALLOWED_HOSTS_PROPERTY = "petstore.api.allowedHosts";
110
111   /**
112    * Request attribute under which an allowed console request carries a {@link String}: a freshly masked token for
113    * this boundary, for a console page to stamp on the form that writes to the API.
114    */
115   public static final String TOKEN_ATTRIBUTE = "org.apache.juneau.petstore.apiCsrfToken";
116
117   private final CsrfBoundary boundary;
118   private final RequestBoundaryFilter filter;
119
120   /**
121    * Constructor.
122    *
123    * <p>
124    * Reads {@value #ALLOWED_HOSTS_PROPERTY} and creates the boundary's per-process token.
125    *
126    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@value #ALLOWED_HOSTS_PROPERTY} holds an entry that is blank or not a bare
127    *    host name.
128    */
129   public PetstoreApiBoundary() {
130      boundary = CsrfBoundary.create()
131         .tokens(CsrfTokens.perProcess())
132         .allowedHosts(allowedHosts(Settings.get().get(ALLOWED_HOSTS_PROPERTY).orElse(null)))
133         .build();
134      filter = new RequestBoundaryFilter(boundary);
135   }
136
137   /**
138    * The host names in an {@value #ALLOWED_HOSTS_PROPERTY} setting.
139    *
140    * @param setting The setting.  Can be <jk>null</jk> or blank (not set).
141    * @return The comma-separated entries, trimmed, blank ones included so the boundary refuses them; empty when the
142    *    setting is not set.
143    */
144   private static String[] allowedHosts(String setting) {
145      if (setting == null || setting.isBlank())
146         return new String[0];
147      return Arrays.stream(setting.split(",", -1)).map(String::trim).toArray(String[]::new);
148   }
149
150   /**
151    * A freshly masked token for a page served to this request to embed.
152    *
153    * <p>
154    * Never creates a session.  The value is different on every call, and every value verifies on this instance only.
155    *
156    * @param req The request whose response will embed the token.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
157    * @return 128 lower-case hex characters.
158    */
159   public String tokenFor(HttpServletRequest req) {
160      return boundary.tokenFor(req);
161   }
162
163   /**
164    * Applies the boundary: a refused request is answered here and never reaches the API.
165    */
166   @Override /* Filter */
167   public void doFilter(ServletRequest req, ServletResponse res, FilterChain chain) throws IOException, ServletException {
168      filter.doFilter(req, res, chain);
169   }
170}
